services.name: Group Tour
services.desc: Illinois Holocaust Museum’s Speakers Bureau of Holocaust Survivors and their descendants offers an opportunity for educators, organizations, civic groups, and others to request event speakers. Hearing directly from a Holocaust Survivor or child/grandchild of a Survivor can leave a lasting impact and has been shown to build empathy and inspire action. Our Museum staff, including educators and leadership, are available to speak at conferences and other events to promote the Museum and Holocaust education. We welcome inquiries from all. services.name: The Living Lessons of Auschwitz
services.desc: On International Holocaust Remembrance Day, we remember Auschwitz, the largest complex of German Nazi concentration camp and killing centers that represents the tragic culmination of years of escalating hatred. It was liberated on January 27, 1945, a date that now marks this solemn international observance. Auschwitz did not emerge out of a vacuum. It was the twisted endpoint of a long, deliberate process in which the Nazi regime consolidated power, dismantled democratic safeguards, silenced opposition, and built an edifice of dehumanization brick by brick.
